question: Does fixed-budget selective target readback preserve task success and reduce information cost when either the original native controller action really executes or an all-zero native arm delta executes but the ACK is unknown?
previous_related_study: 16 state neutral_arm_delta_no_ack only; source commit 7799ede89dc04c2db0ce1379ff4563d553e97a03; result 15/16 success robust-query vs 15/16 mandatory-query and 4 vs 16 target reads; not fresh proof in both worlds

physical_arm_truth.applied_no_ack: Deliver intended converted native arm action to actual simulator controller; observation of delivery to adapter becomes UNKNOWN
physical_arm_truth.neutral_arm_delta_no_ack: Replace intended native arm command with all-zero arm delta; retain source gripper; actual simulator env.step executes; adapter sees UNKNOWN

method_scope: Identical unchanged previous runner algorithm and robust confidence thresholds, except predeclared seed sets, condition switch and protocol/result identity. Absolutely no parameter learning or outcome-dependent tuning.
denominator: 2 frozen externally pretrained PPOs x 8 unique previously unused seeds/task x 2 paired fault truths = 32 task-truth state conditions
primary_readouts: success_once for each controller arm across all 32 conditions
per-world and pooled selective versus mandatory privileged controller target reads
zero-query robust bounded setpoint authorization counts and refusals
paired-task success discordance versus optimistic, no-query bounded and mandatory-query
full condition reach, mixed/failure cases and exact frozen checkpoint identity
limitations: Simulation of delivered or all-zero controller arm action with unknown ACK, not actual network reorder/delay/real robot
One privileged controller target read is used by selective arm on refusal and always arm after fault; no public camera perception, no sensor-free claim
Setpoint position/rotation tolerance is not trajectory safety, contact forces or collision
Identical frozen method and two controller-task families still share Panda controller ABI
True physics state and controller implementation known by experimenter; independent out-of-repository replication absent
Neither midpoint, conditional certificate nor active information gating is an invented general theorem
